ideas.pitch: A lightweight VS Code extension that visualizes and debugs multi-agent tool execution steps directly inside the editor sidebar for BossConsole workflows.
ideas.title: BossConsole VS Code Extension for Agent Tracing
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targeting developer-experience upgrades directly improves BossConsole for real users, making it a high-value practical contribution that judges will immediately appreciate for daily productivity.

ideas.pitch: A Model Context Protocol server integration that allows BossConsole agents to securely query and mutate enterprise databases and local developer tools out of the box.
ideas.title: MCP Server Bridge for BossConsole
ideas.why_it_could_win: Integrations are explicitly requested in the prompt, and building an MCP bridge demonstrates advanced understanding of modern agent interoperability frameworks.

ideas.pitch: An automated regression testing suite that spawns headless AI agents to interact with BossConsole harness components, validating tool-call safety and catching prompt regressions.
ideas.title: BossConsole Autonomous Test Harness
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves a genuine reliability problem for multi-platform AI agent harnesses, reflecting the hard engineering standard seen in top hackathon winners.

ideas.pitch: A security and governance middleware layer for BossConsole that intercepts agent tool calls to enforce role-based access control and block unauthorized shell commands.
ideas.title: BossConsole RBAC and Guardrail Middleware
ideas.why_it_could_win: AI governance and safety are major pain points in multi-agent orchestration, directly aligning with enterprise adoption requirements for BossConsole.

ideas.pitch: A terminal user interface (TUI) built in Python that allows developers to monitor active BossConsole agent sessions, inspect logs, and manage executions directly from the command line.
ideas.title: BossConsole CLI Dashboard TUI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Developer-experience upgrades for CLI and terminal users are extremely practical for open-source maintainers reviewing submissions during a 48-hour sprint.
